title: Maintainability Hygiene
current_summary: Maintainability and local readability are judged through bounded reconstruction inside sound architecture, not mechanical cleanup. Module size, package surfaces, and module headers are inspection signals, not findings by themselves: split or add structure only on concrete responsibility, ownership, unstable-package-surface, reconstruction, or validation-locality evidence, and preserve cohesive long operations where extraction would increase non-local reasoning. The three-family Human Readability investigation validated this (XRef operation.py ~516 LOC and dense_axes.py ~411 LOC are cohesive and locally reconstructable).
next_action: Apply the bounded-reconstruction questions in ordinary reviews; open implementation only on concrete reader/ownership cost plus explicit authority. Add module headers where they give real orientation, not as a uniform mandate; do not run a mechanical cleanup wave. A Human Readability Guide or Sentinel experiment requires separate authorization.
notes: Many low/medium findings are heatmap signals for this concern rather than individual tasks. Reconciled 2026-08-04 with the three-family Human Readability evidence (REVSET-TOPIC-HUMAN-READABILITY, DEC-HUMAN-READABILITY-BOUNDED-RECONSTRUCTION): LOC alone is not a finding, and the module-size/modularization/header FTR records (FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULARIZATION-P4A, FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULE-HEADERS-P5, FTR-MAINTAINER-ENTRYPOINTS-AND-MODULE-BUDGETS-P5) were narrowed accordingly. Real package-surface, ownership, unrelated-responsibility, and agent read-window concerns remain valid.

title: Pipeline YAML Contract vs Callable Signature
current_summary: TODO -- clarify and enforce the boundary among callable signatures, generic binder-reserved fields, BoundStep metadata, and the public YAML step contract. registries/pipeline_step_registry.json mirrors callable parameters, but reserved YAML fields such as name may not reach the callable: the generic binders in pipeline/steps.py (make_builder_target_step, make_frames_target_step) reserve name for the BoundStep label and do not forward it inside **kwargs. title: Domain Boundary Robustness
current_summary: An accepted repository-wide policy fixes how far a domain boundary must defend against malformed or unusual input: robust handling of values reasonably implied by the pandas/NumPy/configuration/metadata/artifact contract, but no promise to contain arbitrary hostile executable Python already in-process; a load-bearing framework-vs-workflow-builder responsibility split; and an enforceable review policy that blocks silent threat-model expansion. ADR-TRUSTED-RUNTIME-AND-POLICY-AUTHORITY (Independent Architecture Review 002, accepted 0 Blocking/0 Important/0 Minor) now extends this into runtime/operator trust: a fixed trusted-runtime/operator precondition; independent payload-trust and pipeline-description-trust dimensions with all four combinations representable; operator-owned security policy supplied outside untrusted pipeline input, narrowing-only; per-policy-kind combination/rejection semantics with a capability-activation timing invariant (safe authorization-preparation normalization is permitted before the decision, activation must wait for it); and sink-capability ownership kept separate from payload normalization. No public profile names, policy API, parser/resource limits, or ingress mechanism are adopted; the accepted Trusted Ingress concept remains explanatory only for those. BUG-UNRESOLVED-HELPER-VALUE-NAN-SEMANTICS-P4A is now Done: the carrier defect is fixed, and the semantic contract is accepted and adopted (Semantic Contract Review 001) -- the derived FK-helper cell is presentation only, never resolution authority; an unresolved lookup and a legitimately resolved empty target value may both display "" while remaining fully distinguishable through the authoritative source FK plus `validate_fk_helpers`; no distinct unresolved-value representation, sentinel, or new type was needed. A separate, narrower residual discovered while resolving that BUG -- a resolved FK whose target payload is itself a missing carrier can still reach the ODS renderer's NaN-blind emptiness check and be serialized as literal "nan" -- was transferred, not left implicit, to BUG-ODS-MISSING-CARRIER-LITERAL-NAN-RENDERING-P4A, which is now also Done: a local, `pd.isna`-aware carrier predicate at the ODS renderer boundary closes both independently reproduced trigger shapes (a resolved FK-helper lookup whose target payload is missing, and an ordinary non-FK csv_dir column), with literal domain `"nan"`, legitimate `""`, and XLSX all confirmed unaffected. No known carrier leak remains open at this boundary. `FTR-MINIMAL-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A` (New, decision-ready; a431182) recorded the Phase-D current-state inventory and recommended MVP category set (String/Boolean/Number/Missing, Error deferred; Integer-vs-Float bounded-deferred) with no runtime, ADR, or Project Memory change of its own. A follow-up scope-hygiene pass (0f07368) then tightened that FTR's formula and Date/Time wording and split a dedicated deferred anchor, `FTR-FORMULA-INGRESS-ROUNDTRIP-WHITELIST-P5`, for durable formula-preservation/roundtrip constraints (strict allowlist, feature-owned contracts, no general Excel/OpenFormula compatibility promise, the FK-helper emit-does-not-imply-preserve precedent) so a future implementation agent cannot accidentally widen Slice 1 into formula support.
next_action: Phase D's Minimal Internal Value Model implementation slices (D1-D3 in FTR-MINIMAL-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A) may begin: formulas are explicitly out of scope (tracked separately, deferred, by FTR-FORMULA-INGRESS-ROUNDTRIP-WHITELIST-P5) and Date/Time is explicitly out of this first slice but expected as an early Phase-D follow-up slice, unlike Formula. Security-policy representation, parser/resource limits, other sink-local work (e.g. the XLSX leading-`=` formula gap), the FTR-PIPELINE-DOTTED-EXTENSION-SURFACE-P4A assessment, and the public run_pipeline boundary decision remain independently authorizable work and must not be merged into Phase D's scope.
notes: Steering field for the FTR-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS-P4A evidence-gated umbrella, DEC-DOMAIN-BOUNDARY-ROBUSTNESS, and now DEC-TRUSTED-RUNTIME-AND-POLICY-AUTHORITY. Raised by the escalating adversarial acceptance rounds on the Axis Mapping resolver. Complements ADR-DOMAIN-OWNS-VALIDATION-WRITERS-STAY-DUMB (validation ownership) and ADR-VISIBLE-CELL-TYPING-STRING-SUBSTRATE (carrier payload typing, unchanged and not reopened by the new ADR, and not reopened by the unresolved-helper carrier fix or its semantic contract either); it governs in-memory value-object boundaries and failure atomicity, not the persistence projection. The new ADR was extracted narrowly from accepted Technical Concept 001 (Trusted Ingress, Internal Value Model, and Runtime Security Profiles), which remains explanatory only for its illustrative profile names, internal value/lifecycle taxonomy, boundary-implementation mechanics, and FTR candidate map. See SIG-ACT-UNRESOLVED-HELPER-CARRIER-FIX-ACCEPTED for the first runtime slice and SIG-ACT-UNRESOLVED-HELPER-SEMANTICS-CLOSED for the semantic-contract acceptance, adoption, and BUG closure with residual transfer. See SIG-ACT-VALUE-MODEL-SCOPE-BOUNDED for the Phase-D scope-hygiene pass and the new deferred formula-policy FTR.
